metadata.title: Bangladesh crop management reference
metadata.authority: Bangladesh Agro-Meteorological Information Service (BAMIS), Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE)
metadata.scope: Retrieval reference for crop guidance. Rates below are transcribed from the linked BAMIS package pages and retain their stated crop/season/unit context. They are not personalized soil-test recommendations. Missing fields are explicitly unverified.
metadata.fertilizerCaution: BARC Fertilizer Recommendation Guide 2024 requires soil-test interpretation and location/AEZ context. Do not use blanket rates where soil fertility and location have not been checked.
metadata.trainingNote: This is source-linked deterministic retrieval, not machine-learning training or fine-tuning.

lifecycle.value: BAMIS package distinguishes long-duration (>150 days) and short-duration (<150 days) lowland Boro types; variety-specific crop duration should be checked in the calendar/seed label.

timing.value: See the BAMIS Boro package and the district calendar; timing varies by variety and district.

water.value: BAMIS package: do not assume continuous standing water is always needed; maintain 2–3 cm up to 12–15 days after transplanting, then alternate wetting and drying with 5–7 cm water depth until panicle emergence; maintain 2–5 cm from panicle formation to grain hardening.

fertilizer.value: For lowland long-duration (>150-day) Boro, BAMIS lists per bigha: urea 40 kg, TSP 13 kg, MP 22 kg, gypsum 15 kg, zinc sulphate 1.5 kg. It says apply TSP, MP, gypsum and zinc at final land preparation; split urea into thirds: basal, tillering, and 5–7 days before panicle initiation. Short-duration/medium-land rates differ; consult the source package.

timing.value: Ideal sowing: 15–30 November; BAMIS says it may be extended to 15–20 December.

water.value: BAMIS generally calls for 2–3 irrigations: first 17–21 days after sowing (three-leaf stage), second 50–55 days (start of tillering), and third 75–80 days (grain formation). First two should be light irrigations.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS package lists per hectare at final land preparation: urea 150–175 kg, TSP 135–150 kg, potash 100–110 kg, gypsum 110–125 kg; additionally boric acid 6.5 kg/ha and zinc sulphate 12.5 kg/ha. For irrigated fields it separately says apply 75–90 kg urea/ha at three-leaf stage with first irrigation. Confirm local soil and package applicability before use.

compost.value: Apply 7.5–10 tonnes of cow dung/compost per hectare at the beginning of land preparation.

sources.title: Wheat package and practices of cultivation

timing.value: BAMIS: Rabi sowing 15 October–15 November; Kharif-1 sowing 15 February–15 March.

water.value: BAMIS schedule: irrigate around 15–20 days (4–6 leaves), 30–35 days (8–12 leaves), 60–70 days (cob emergence), and 85–89 days (grain formation). This is a stage schedule, not a fixed volume; adjust for rainfall and soil moisture, and prevent waterlogging.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS product rates in kg/ha (Rabi / Kharif-1): urea 172–312 / 216–268; TSP 168–216 / 132–216; MP 96–144 / 72–120; gypsum 144–168 / 96–144; zinc sulphate 10–15 / 7–12; boric acid 5–7 / 5–7 as required. It directs 1/3 urea basal and the remainder in two top dressings at 25–30 and 40–50 days after germination. Ranges are broad and require local/soil-test selection.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 4–6 tonnes of cow dung/organic manure per hectare for both Rabi and Kharif-1.

sources.title: Maize package and practices of cultivation

timing.value: BAMIS lists Ashwin–Poush (approximately mid-September to mid-December) as a suitable sowing period.

water.value: BAMIS recommends irrigation when needed and mentions irrigation during sowing/dry conditions; it does not provide a fixed water volume. Check soil moisture and rainfall rather than irrigating to a fixed amount.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 500 g, DAP/TSP 600 g, MOP 500 g, gypsum 600 g. It also lists urea 80–100 g and MOP 80–100 g at 3 weeks, then again at 6 weeks after sowing. Reduce amounts when soil fertility has been checked or fertilizer already applied; confirm the DAP/TSP alternative in the original package.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 40 kg dung/compost per শতক (century).

timing.value: BAMIS: sowing varies by variety; January is the general Rabi period. Its source page lists distinct summer, winter and year-round varieties, so choose a locally recommended variety and season.

water.value: BAMIS advises light irrigation after transplanting and irrigation after top-dressed fertilizer; it says summer crops need more frequent irrigation, while monsoon crops usually need less. Use furrows/drains and avoid waterlogging; no fixed water volume is given.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 1.20 kg, TSP 810 g, MOP/potash 970 g. Apply all compost, TSP and 360 g potash at final land preparation. It describes urea top-dressings after transplanting at 10, 25 and 40 days, with remaining potash split; check the source page and local DAE for the exact split before use.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 40 kg rotten cow dung/compost per শতক (century).

timing.value: BAMIS lists the first week of mid-October to November (Rabi) as a suitable planting period.

water.value: BAMIS recommends 4–5 cm straw/rice-straw mulch to reduce moisture loss, irrigation when needed, and stopping irrigation about 3 weeks before harvest. The frequency text on the page is unclear, so no fixed interval is used here.
water.unit: mulch depth; stop irrigation 3 weeks before harvest

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per hectare: urea 200 kg, TSP 250 kg, potash 250 kg, gypsum 110 kg. It says apply TSP, gypsum and half the urea/potash at final land preparation; apply the remainder in two equal splits at 25 and 50 days after sowing. Soil-test/local selection still required.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 5 tonnes compost per hectare (also 20 kg per শতক).

timing.value: BAMIS lists Boishakh–Jaistha (approximately April–May) as suitable sowing time.

water.value: BAMIS says rainfall may make irrigation unnecessary at planting; irrigate only when rainfall is absent and soil moisture is low, and drain excess water promptly. No fixed amount is given.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per hectare: urea 300 kg, TSP 270 kg, potash 230 kg, gypsum 110 kg and zinc 2.5 kg. It describes basal application and top-dressing stages around 50, 80 and 100 days; the English translation is unclear about exact split quantities, so confirm the original package/local DAE before applying.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 10 tonnes compost per hectare (also 20–40 kg per শতক); the stated area conversions do not align exactly, so use the original local package/soil-test guidance and do not scale automatically.
compost.unit: source-reported tonnes/ha and kg per শতক; conversion needs review

timing.value: BAMIS lists Ashwin (September–October) and Poush (December–January) sowing periods. Variety and local planting conditions matter.

water.value: BAMIS advises irrigation according to soil moisture, generally 2–3 times after about two weeks, and quick drainage of excess rainwater. The source does not state a fixed volume; avoid excess water.

fertilizer.value: The BAMIS page gives per-plant amounts in its table (urea 400–500 g, TSP 500 g, MOP 450–500 g, gypsum 250 g, zinc and boron 20 g each). It describes manure and selected fertilizers per planting pit and monthly urea/MOP after planting; quantities are plant/pit-based, not per hectare. Check the source page and DAE for the correct sequence before use.
fertilizer.unit: g per plant/pit as stated; not an area rate

compost.value: BAMIS describes 15 kg dung manure per planting pit 15–20 days before planting. Do not scale per hectare without plant spacing and confirmed pit guidance.

timing.value: BAMIS lists Bhadra–Ashwin (approximately mid-August to mid-October) as a suitable sowing period.

water.value: BAMIS describes irrigation around 25–30 days after planting, again around 40–45 days/before flowering, and once before seed filling; adjust for rainfall and soil moisture. No fixed volume is specified.

timing.value: BAMIS lists Kharif-1: 15 February–15 March; Kharif-2: 15 July–15 September; and Rabi: September–October. Variety matters; BARI pepper-1 is described as year-round, while other varieties have seasonal suitability.

water.value: BAMIS advises irrigation when moisture is insufficient, maintaining moisture during flowering and fruit growth, and providing drainage after heavy rain. Its translated page does not specify a reliable volume or universal interval.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 1.6 kg, TSP 1 kg, potash 600 g and gypsum 200 g. It says dung, TSP and part of the potash are basal, with later splits; wording on exact split amounts is unclear in the English source, so confirm the application schedule with the Bangla source/DAE before use.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 40 kg dung per শতক (century).

timing.value: District calendar dates are available for Cumilla and Chattogram only. BAMIS regional bulletins also describe mid-October to mid-November as an optimum general sowing period; use the local crop calendar and variety.

water.value: BAMIS says use residual soil moisture; if moisture is inadequate, apply light irrigation. A regional bulletin suggests irrigation around 20–25 days before flowering and 50–55 days during fruiting when needed. This is conditional timing, not a fixed volume.

fertilizer.value: A BAMIS germination-stage advisory lists per hectare: urea 125–150 kg, TSP 170–180 kg and MOP 85–100 kg before sowing; it is an advisory note, not an individualized or soil-test recommendation. The cited advisory's cow-dung unit is unclear, so no manure quantity is reported.
fertilizer.unit: kg/ha; product rates; regional stage advisory

timing.value: BAMIS lists Ashwin–Kartik (approximately mid-September to mid-November) as a suitable sowing period; it lists particular improved varieties for Rabi.

water.value: BAMIS advises irrigation when moisture is insufficient and mentions irrigation about every 15 days during winter/dry conditions. This is conditional guidance with no fixed volume; check actual soil moisture and rainfall.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 200 g, TSP 1 kg, potash 400 g and boric acid 40 g. Apply compost/dung, TSP and half urea/potash at final land preparation; the remaining urea/potash in two equal splits during weeks 3 and 5 after sowing. Soil-test/local adjustment is needed.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 40–50 kg dung/compost per শতক (century).

timing.value: BAMIS lists Shravan–Kartik (approximately August–October) and Falgun–Jaistha (approximately February–May) as suitable sowing periods.

water.value: BAMIS says bottle gourd is sensitive to water shortage; in dry season, irrigation may be needed every 5–7 days. Use furrow irrigation rather than flooding the whole field, and drain excess rainwater.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 2 kg, TSP 1.6 kg, potash 1.2 kg, boron 10 g. It describes basal application and splitting remaining urea/potash in four rounds; check local soil and source package before use.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 40 kg dung/compost per শতক (century).

pumpkin.identityNote: This record applies only to sweet pumpkin (BAMIS crop page 32). It must not be used for ash gourd or another pumpkin type; clarify the crop identity first.

timing.value: For sweet pumpkin only, BAMIS lists Kartik–Agrahayan (approximately October–November) as a suitable sowing period.

water.value: For sweet pumpkin, BAMIS says it is sensitive to water shortage; irrigate in the furrow rather than flooding the whole field. In dry season irrigation may be needed every 5–7 days; drain excess rainwater.

fertilizer.value: For sweet pumpkin only, BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 2 kg, TSP 1.6 kg and potash 1.2 kg. It describes basal fertilizer and later split applications; verify the exact schedule and soil-test need locally.

compost.value: For sweet pumpkin only, BAMIS lists 40 kg compost per শতক (century), equivalent in the same table to 10 tonnes/ha.
compost.unit: kg per শতক / tonnes per hectare as source-listed

pulses.identityNote: ‘Pulse’ is a crop group, not one crop. Lentil, mung bean, chickpea and mashkalai have different crop calendars and input requirements. Ask the farmer to identify the pulse before giving a crop-specific rate.

sources.title: Pulse crop list; crop-specific guidance differs

turnip.identityNote: No crop-specific Bangladesh government cultivation package was verified for this catalog entry. Do not substitute radish or another root crop's rates.

lifecycle.value: The BAMIS page citing BARI Agricultural Technology Handbook (2017) lists 65- and 100-day varieties. It also says harvest may occur 60–75 days after planting; timing depends on variety.

timing.value: BAMIS/BARI source: sow seed in Bhadra–Ashwin (mid-August to mid-October) and transplant around Kartik–Agrahayan (mid-November to December); the page also notes August–September as an appropriate sowing time. Match the selected variety and local district calendar.

water.value: BAMIS describes cauliflower as suitable on land with irrigation and drainage facilities; no fixed irrigation volume/schedule was verified.

sources.organization: BAMIS / DAE, citing BARI Agricultural Technology Handbook (6th ed., 2017)
sources.title: Cauliflower cultivation information

water.value: BAMIS says early varieties may need about 400–600 mm well-distributed rainfall during the vegetative period; this is not a universal irrigation target. Avoid heavy rain/waterlogging and alternating very wet/dry conditions; soil moisture guidance is 65–80% of field capacity.
water.unit: mm rainfall for early varieties; field-capacity fraction

timing.value: BAMIS describes seed sowing for Kharif in February–March and for Rabi in July–August; source wording and variety distinctions should be checked with local DAE before planting.

water.value: BAMIS says irrigate lightly after sowing and then as needed; it does not supply a fixed volume. Avoid over-irrigation and use field moisture/rainfall to guide irrigation.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per শতক (century): urea 970 g, TSP 890 g, potash 610 g, gypsum 440 g. It instructs to apply compost/dung, TSP, gypsum and half of urea/potash at final land preparation; the remaining half urea/potash in two installments at 25 and 50 days. Confirm the source page with DAE because its English translation has ambiguous wording.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 32–40 kg dung per শতক (century).

timing.value: BAMIS page gives nursery/transplanting guidance; a district-specific crop lifecycle was not extracted for this record.

water.value: BAMIS says to give light irrigation after fertilizer application; a full seasonal volume/schedule is not verified in this record.

fertilizer.value: BAMIS lists per hectare: urea 350 kg, TSP 250 kg, potash 250 kg. It says apply dung and TSP during land preparation; urea and MOP are top-dressed in two rounds around 20–25 and 30–40 days after transplanting. Soil-test/local applicability must be checked.

compost.value: BAMIS lists 5–10 tonnes compost per hectare.

timing.value: BAMIS lists Ashwin–Kartik (approximately mid-September to mid-November) as suitable sowing time.

water.value: BAMIS discusses irrigation when moisture is insufficient; fixed crop water volume was not verified.
